Subject: Proposal: GPU safety-stock, phased decommit triggers & commit term for Aurora (DEAL-4521)

Team —

Aurora has asked for a 24-month reserved capacity commitment but is pushing hard on price protection given the volatility in GPU spot and procurement market. They shared a usage forecast (attached) that has a fairly spiky Q1-Q3 profile for year 1. We need a concise internal proposal to take into the next commercial call with them next week.

Key asks from me:
- Recommend a safety-stock (buffer) % to protect against short-notice surges.
- Phased decommit / clawback mechanics if their usage falls below thresholds.
- Discount bands vs committed units + approval thresholds (who signs off for >25% off list?).
- One-slide summary and an ask to Finance/Legal for the approval path.

Attachments: Aurora_usage_forecast.xlsx, Aurora_SLA_requirements.pdf

Please respond with numbers and the minimal executive ask by EOD Monday so I can synthesize before the call.

Thanks,

Tessa Morgan
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Proposal: GPU safety-stock, phased decommit triggers & commit term for Aurora (DEAL-4521)

Tessa —

Thanks for the heads-up. I built a quick sizing model (attached) and ran three scenarios: conservative, baseline (customer forecast), and optimistic. High-level takeaways:

- Baseline (use their median forecast): 180 reserved A100-equivalent units across two regions; peak concurrency risk during onboarding months.
- Safety-stock recommendation: 15% buffer over baseline (adds ~27 A100-eq units) to keep 99th percentile latency SLOs intact without immediate autoscale.
- Cost impact: At current GPU-cost assumptions, 15% buffer increases committed monthly spend by ~18%. If GPU market price drops 20%, effective unit-cost advantage improves and the buffer becomes less costly.

Recommended commercial construct to offer Aurora:
1) 24-month term, with a 15% initial safety-stock added to committed units for months 1-6 (absorbs onboarding spikes).
2) Phased decommit: after month 6, allow two staged decommit windows at month 9 and month 15 if trailing 90-day usage < 70% of committed (each decommit reduces committed units by up to 20%).
3) Price protection: introduce a GPU-cost indexation clause that permits limited pass-through adjustments if market GPU list moves > 25% for 3 consecutive months.

Approvals needed: discounts up to 20% off list — Sales lead OK; 20-35% needs Finance director signoff; >35% requires CFO/VP approval.

Attaching sizing_model_v1.csv with the scenario numbers.

Marcus Lin
Head of Capacity Planning | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Proposal: GPU safety-stock, phased decommit triggers & commit term for Aurora (DEAL-4521)

Folks —

Couple of legal/procurement items to bake into the proposal so we don't leave open escalations during contracting:

- Decommit windows need explicit notice windows and measurement method. Proposal: 30 days' notice plus trailing 90-day rolling avg to determine usage bands.
- If we add an indexation clause, limit pass-through to cost swings attributable to HW procurement only (exclude energy/third-party network fees).
- Consider a temporary penalty-free phased decommit for the first 6 weeks post-onboarding (we commonly see big onboarding drops). After that, any decommit below 70% should trigger a small decommit fee (e.g., 5% of monthly committed spend for two months) to avoid gaming.
- Approval path: anything that changes the discount grid or indexation thresholds must go through the commercial exceptions board (ComEx). We should prepare a one-page deck for ComEx that includes: expected committed ARR, unit economics delta with buffer, and projected cost exposure under the 3 market scenarios Marcus produced.

I can draft the wording for the phased decommit clause and the notice/measuring language. Marcus — can you include the projected dollar exposure lines for the three price movement scenarios (flat, -20%, +30%)? Naomi — we'll need a clear signoff template for finance gating.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Ops & Contracts | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Proposal: GPU safety-stock, phased decommit triggers & commit term for Aurora (DEAL-4521)

All —

I ran a quick pricing-sensitivity table using Marcus's model. Summary below (rounded):

Assumptions: baseline unit cost = $X per A100-eq token-hour (confidential). Committed baseline = 180 units.

Scenarios (monthly committed spend delta vs no-buffer baseline):
- Baseline (no buffer): $0 (reference)
- +10% buffer: +~11% committed spend
- +15% buffer: +~18% committed spend (Marcus's rec)
- +25% buffer: +~28% committed spend

Price movement sensitivity (if list GPU price moves):
- GPU price -20%: net spend with 15% buffer ~ +3% vs baseline (buffer cost largely absorbed)
- GPU price +30%: net spend with 15% buffer ~ +28% vs baseline (material hit)

Approval thresholds (to align with your ask):
- Discount <= 20%: Sales + Revenue Manager
- Discount 21-35%: Finance Director signoff required (Naomi or delegate)
- Discount > 35%: VP Finance + Commercial Exceptions Board (ComEx) approval + exec memo

We should also be explicit about who owns the indexation calculation (ops/finance). I recommend Ops publishes a monthly GPU index number with finance verifying quarterly. That keeps the math auditable.

If we land on the 24-month term and 15% buffer, I can pre-prepare the finance approval package (expected delta by quarter) — I'll need Marcus's three scenario dollar lines and Karthik's proposed clause language to include in ComEx packet.

Naomi Feldman

Julie / Aurora team —

Thanks for the productive discussion earlier this week. Per our internal alignment, here is the recommended approach we'd like to take to balance Aurora's SLO needs with unit-economics and our capacity planning: 

Proposal (summary):
- Commit term: 24 months.
- Committed units: baseline 180 A100-eq + 15% safety-stock for onboarding months 1-6 (net buffer = 27 units).
- Phased decommit: two evaluation windows at month 9 and month 15. If trailing 90-day usage < 70% of committed, Aurora may decommit up to 20% at each window. 30 days' notice required; measurement based on trailing 90-day rolling average.
- Decommit fee: to avoid adverse selection, a two-month 5% committed-spend smoothing charge applies to any decommit below 70% after onboarding grace.
- GPU-cost indexation: pass-through limited to HW procurement price swings >25% sustained for 3 months; pass-through scope limited to HW only.
- Discount grid: standard discount to land the deal at the above construct; any discount >25% will need Finance Director signoff and ComEx review for >35%.

Next steps:
1) Julie — can you confirm CloudScale is comfortable with the 15% buffer sizing for the first 6 months and can commit to the SKU mix for provisioning?
2) Aurora — can you confirm the 24-month term is acceptable in principle so we can circulate a draft SOW and ComEx packet early next week?

I've CC'd Marcus/Naomi/Karthik who will provide the ComEx packet and clause wording once we have a thumbs-up.

Best,

Tessa Morgan
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
